netWorthTrend.title: Net Worth Trend
netWorthTrend.intro: Shows your business's net worth (all assets − debts) as of each month-end, so you can see at a glance whether you're growing over time.
netWorthTrend.introTabs: Use the tabs to view the same net worth through a different lens: inflation-adjusted (real), US dollars, euros, or grams of gold.

lensDesc.nominal: The plain amount in your main currency.
lensDesc.reel: Inflation-adjusted: real purchasing power in today's lira. Even if the number stays the same, its buying power may have changed.
lensDesc.usd: How many US dollars your net worth is worth (at that month's rate).
lensDesc.eur: How many euros your net worth is worth (at that month's rate).
lensDesc.altin: How many grams of gold your net worth is worth (at that month's gold price).

netWorthTrend.noData: No data yet for this view

insight.realUp: In {{lens}} terms, your net worth rose {{pct}}% in real terms over the last {{months}} months (nominal {{nom}}%).
insight.realDown: Nominal {{nom}}%, but against {{lens}} your net worth eroded {{pct}}% in real terms.
insight.debtLighter: Your debt looks flat nominally, but against {{lens}} its real burden eased by {{pct}}%.

netWorthTrend.sparseNote: Records are sparse in the earliest months; these values are reconstructed backward from today (derived).
netWorthTrend.conversionIncomplete: Exchange rates could not be loaded; balances without a rate were excluded. Values may be incomplete.
netWorthTrend.footnote: Past months are recalculated backward from today's records. Balances of inactive/archived contacts, personnel and accounts, as well as inventory/fixed-asset value, are NOT included in net worth; only the cash effect of payments/collections to them is counted. Deleted transactions and undated openings may not reflect exactly in history. Today's value matches your current net worth exactly. The monthly CHANGE follows the same rule: transactions of passive/archived contacts, staff and accounts are excluded — so a month's change can differ from the same month in the Income-Expense report (that report includes archived records).
netWorthTrend.footnoteFx: Inflation, USD, EUR and gold data come from the Turkish Central Bank (TCMB / EVDS); each month uses its own period rate.

incomeExpenseLens.title: VALUATION VIEW
incomeExpenseLens.panelSubtitle: Review past income and expenses using the exchange rate or inflation level from that time. This helps you see more clearly whether your revenue or expenses truly increased or decreased.

description.nominal: Shows amounts exactly as they were recorded.
description.reel: Adjusts amounts for inflation to today's purchasing power.
description.usd: Shows amounts using the dollar rate on the transaction day.
description.eur: Shows amounts using the euro rate on the transaction day.
description.altin: Shows amounts using the gram-gold value on the transaction day.

note.reel: CPI is monthly; each day uses the latest index published for its transaction month.
note.usd: Uses the CBRT indicative selling rate; holidays use the previous business day.
note.eur: Uses the CBRT indicative selling rate; holidays use the previous business day.
note.altin: Uses the CBRT 11:00 XAU TRY/gram reference; holidays use the previous business day.

help.accessibilityLabel: How is the price change report calculated?
help.title: What does this report show?
help.subtitle: How price changes affect your purchase costs
help.outcomeTitle: The cucumber price ended the month lower
help.transitionBody: This count compares each purchase price with the previous purchase, not just the start and end of the month:
help.transitionSummary: There were 2 increases and 4 decreases during the month. The final price was still below the first price, so the month ended with a net decrease.
help.referenceTitle: First, a reference price is selected
help.referenceBody: The latest valid purchase price before the selected period is used. If there is no earlier purchase, the first purchase price in the period becomes the reference. In this example there was no earlier purchase, so the reference is TRY 40/kg.
help.calculationTitle: How are TRY 1,875 of savings calculated?
help.calculationIntro: A total of 177 kg of cucumbers was purchased in July. Each purchase group is compared separately with the TRY 40 reference price.
help.conclusion: If all 177 kg had cost TRY 40, the total would have been TRY 7,080. The changing prices produced an actual total of TRY 5,205, which is TRY 1,875 less.
help.whyTitle: Isn't the move from TRY 30 to TRY 35 an increase?
help.whyBody: Yes, it is an increase compared with the previous purchase. But TRY 35 is still below the TRY 40 reference price, so it is shown as a price increase while still producing savings against the reference.
help.changeCountBody: Compares each price with the previous purchase price.
help.savingsViewBody: Compares every purchase price with the period's TRY 40 reference price.
help.note: Estimated savings is not profit or cash income. It is the difference from what the same quantity would have cost at the reference price. Returns are excluded.
